title: Technology Sector Update for 06/25/2018: CIEN,COR,MSFT,QUIK,XRX
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT -2.52%
AAPL -1.93%
IBM -1.64%
CSCO -2.72%
GOOG -3.26%
Technology stocks were sharply lower Monday as prospects for a global trade war continue to escalate, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing almost 2.6% in value while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 3.7% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Ciena Corp ( CIEN ) was more than 3% higher Monday afternoon, easing from a 5% rise earlier in the session, that followed analysts at Morgan Stanley raising their investment recommendation for the networking equipment manufacturer to Overweight from Equalweight. Separately, CoreSite Realty Corp ( COR ) said it will soon be launching an enhanced open-cloud exchange platform using Ciena's Blue Planet multi-domain service orchestrator. The CoreSite exchange platform should be operational in the next few weeks, the company said, and will provide its data center clients with improved functionally and several new features, including support for a single-port connections to Microsoft's ( MSFT ) Azure ExpresRoute.
In other sector news:
- QuickLogic ( QUIK ) was little changed in recent afternoon trading, giving back a more than 3% gain soon after Monday's opening bell that followed the chipmaker granting a master technology license deal to C-Sky Microsystems Co for its ArcticPro embedded field-programmable gate array integrated circuit technology. C-Sky plans to market ArcticPro along with its 32-bit high performance low-power embedded CPUs, also integrating the intellectual property in new system-on-chip designs.
- Xerox ( XRX ) dropped to an 18-month low on Monday, sinking over 2% to its worst share price since December 2016 at $25.69 apiece, after CEO John Visentin said Fujifilm's suit was a "nothing more than a desperate and misguided negotiating ploy to save their takeover attempt." In a letter last week to Fujifilm board chairman Shigetaka Komori, Visentin also said the internal accounting issues at the companies' Fuji Xerox partnership that scuttled their proposed merger "were a result of (Fuji's) mismanagement," later adding his company has an "enormous opportunity" to sell its products directly into the Asia-Pacific markets under the Xerox brand.
